quote: Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.
source: Rosa Luxemburg, The Russian Revolution, ch. 6, The Problem of Dictatorship (trans. Bertram D. Wolfe, 1940)

evidence.where: The Marxists Internet Archive transcription of The Russian Revolution, chapter 6, read for this passage. It prints the sentence verbatim with its terminal stop, immediately after Freedom only for the supporters of the government, only for the members of one party, however numerous they may be, is no freedom at all. The archive's index page for the work names Bertram Wolfe as translator and Workers Age Publishers, New York, 1940 as the edition, and lists chapter 6 as The Problem of Dictatorship.
evidence.edition: trans. Bertram D. Wolfe, Workers Age Publishers, New York, 1940; the manuscript was written in 1918 and first published by Paul Levi in 1922
evidence.locator: chapter 6, The Problem of Dictatorship, in the passage on freedom under one party

reason: The proposal hedged on the chapter, and the chapter is now located: chapter 6, The Problem of Dictatorship, in Wolfe's 1940 wording, with the preceding sentence the proposal named. Luxemburg stands at one for the year from February and is neither banned nor at cap. The line is a written argument rather than a speech, so it is in scope, and it states the plainest test of wanting the truth without any image that would need a warning.
